name: MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines v2.0
description: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) Technology Risk Management (TRM) Guidelines v2.0 (2021) overlay. Mandatory for all MAS-regulated financial institutions in Singapore — banks, insurers, capital market intermediaries, and payment services providers. Prescriptive technology risk governance framework covering IT governance, application security, cyber surveillance, vendor management, and data management. AI-specific: MAS FEAT Principles (2018) and MAS AI governance guidance apply as companion obligations for FIs deploying AI/ML in customer-facing or risk-decisive functions.
regulated_entities: MAS-regulated financial institutions — banks, insurers, capital markets intermediaries, payment services providers, and other entities holding a MAS licence or approval

evidence_requirements: IT and technology risk governance framework documented and approved by board of directors (MAS TRM §3.1)
Board-level oversight of technology risk demonstrated — board and senior management roles in technology risk defined (MAS TRM §3.2)
Technology Risk Management function established with documented responsibilities (MAS TRM §3.3)
AI/ML governance policy established for FIs using AI in customer-facing or risk-decisive functions — MAS FEAT Principles documented compliance
Chief Information Officer (CIO) and/or Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) appointed with defined responsibilities (MAS TRM §3.3)
Technology risk ownership assigned to senior management with board reporting line
Accountability for AI systems documented — named individual or team for each deployed AI model in production
Technology governance committee meeting records — evidence of senior management oversight
GOV-02.framework_reference: MAS TRM §3.2–3.3 (Board and Senior Management Responsibilities)

evidence_requirements: Technology risk assessment conducted at least annually and on material changes (MAS TRM §5.1)
Risk appetite for technology and cyber risk defined by board and operationalized (MAS TRM §5.2)
Risk assessment covers AI system risks — algorithmic bias, model drift, adversarial inputs, data poisoning
Residual risk formally accepted and documented by appropriate risk owner
GOV-03.framework_reference: MAS TRM §5.1–5.2 (Technology Risk Assessment and Appetite)

evidence_requirements: Human oversight configuration for AI systems documented — particularly for credit decisions, fraud detection, customer advice, and other regulated functions
MAS FEAT Principles compliance documented — Fairness, Ethics, Accountability, and Transparency controls for AI used in customer-impacting decisions
Human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop oversight level determined by regulatory impact of AI decision
Override and contestation mechanism available for AI-assisted customer decisions
GOV-04.framework_reference: MAS TRM §5 (Risk Management); MAS FEAT Principles §Accountability

evidence_requirements: Technology asset inventory maintained covering all systems in scope of MAS TRM (MAS TRM §4.1)
AI/ML model inventory maintained — model name, version, deployment date, intended use, owner, data inputs, risk classification
Critical systems identified with enhanced controls and recovery capability
Asset inventory reviewed at least annually and updated on material changes
Third-party technology components and tools inventoried (MAS TRM §11.1)
AI/ML APIs, model hosting services, and third-party model providers documented in vendor inventory
Software bill of materials (SBOM) maintained for critical systems including AI pipelines
Technology outsourcing register maintained with risk classification for each vendor
Data classification policy implemented — sensitivity levels defined and applied to customer and operational data (MAS TRM §13.1)
AI training data documented — sources, quality controls, bias assessment, representativeness
Data handling procedures mapped to classification level — access controls, encryption, retention, disposal
Customer data used in AI/ML models — consent and purpose limitation documented per Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
Technology vendor risk assessment conducted before engagement and periodically thereafter (MAS TRM §11.2)
AI/ML model providers and cloud AI service providers assessed for concentration risk, data sovereignty, and security posture
Outsourced AI functions: risk assessment, contractual protections, and exit planning documented (MAS TRM §11.3)
Vendor due diligence records maintained with risk ratings and remediation tracking
Technology risk classification applied to each system — critical, important, or general systems (MAS TRM §5.1)
AI systems classified based on regulatory function, customer impact, and failure consequences
Higher-risk AI systems (credit, fraud, customer advice) subject to enhanced controls and oversight
Risk profile updated on material changes to system, data inputs, or operating environment
Privileged access management (PAM) controls implemented for critical systems including AI infrastructure (MAS TRM §7.1)
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced for remote access and privileged accounts (MAS TRM §7.1)
Access reviews conducted at least semi-annually — AI system access included
Separation of duties enforced for AI model development, validation, and production deployment
PR-01.framework_reference: MAS TRM §7.1 (Access Control and Privileged Access)

evidence_requirements: Principle of least privilege applied to all system accounts including AI service accounts (MAS TRM §7.1)
AI model permissions scoped to production data necessary for declared function — no broad access
Service account permissions reviewed on AI system deployments and updates
Permission scope documented in access control records and system security plans
Software integrity verification implemented — checksums or signatures verified for third-party AI components (MAS TRM §7.3)
Application change management process requires security review for AI model updates (MAS TRM §6.1)
Third-party AI component authenticity verified before deployment — provenance chain documented
Patch and update management process applied to AI libraries, SDKs, and model serving infrastructure
Customer and sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit in AI processing pipelines (MAS TRM §13.2)
Data masking or anonymisation applied to non-production AI training environments
AI model outputs involving customer data reviewed for inadvertent data disclosure
Data loss prevention (DLP) controls applied to AI system outputs and logs containing sensitive data
Audit logging implemented for all critical system actions including AI inference requests and model changes (MAS TRM §9.1)
Logs include: timestamp, user/system identity, action, data accessed, and outcome
Log retention minimum 1 year online, 5 years total for regulated financial activities (MAS TRM §9.1)
Audit logs protected from modification — integrity controls evidenced
PR-05.framework_reference: MAS TRM §9.1 (Security Monitoring and Audit Logging)

evidence_requirements: Configuration management process documented — baseline configurations for AI infrastructure and model serving (MAS TRM §6.1)
Change advisory board (CAB) or equivalent approves material AI system changes
Configuration baselines maintained and drift detection in place (MAS TRM §6.2)
Production AI model configuration changes require documented approval and testing evidence
PR-06.framework_reference: MAS TRM §6.1–6.2 (IT Project and Change Management)

evidence_requirements: TLS 1.2 or higher enforced for all AI API communications — certificate management documented (MAS TRM §7.2)
Network segmentation applied to AI infrastructure — AI processing environments isolated from untrusted networks
Mutual authentication enforced for inter-system AI service communications in production
Encryption key management documented including rotation schedule (MAS TRM §13.2)
Secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) applied to AI applications — includes security code review and testing (MAS TRM §7.2)
Input validation implemented for all AI system interfaces exposed to customers or third parties
Penetration testing conducted annually for customer-facing AI systems (MAS TRM §7.4)
Vulnerability assessment program includes AI model serving infrastructure
Security information and event management (SIEM) deployed with coverage of AI infrastructure (MAS TRM §9.1)
AI model performance monitoring implemented — tracks accuracy, drift, anomalous output rates
Behavioural anomaly detection for AI system usage — unusual query volumes, unexpected output patterns
Monitoring alerts reviewed and triaged — evidence of SOC or equivalent operational monitoring
DE-01.framework_reference: MAS TRM §9.1–9.2 (Cyber Surveillance and Security Monitoring)

evidence_requirements: Configuration drift detection implemented for critical AI infrastructure — alerts on unauthorised changes (MAS TRM §6.2)
Integrity monitoring in place for AI model files and serving infrastructure
Drift alerts reviewed within defined SLA — evidence of alert review and disposition records
DE-02.framework_reference: MAS TRM §6.2 (Change Detection and Configuration Monitoring)

evidence_requirements: Technology risk compliance review conducted periodically — AI systems included in scope (MAS TRM §5.1)
Internal audit coverage of AI systems and technology risk controls
Compliance deviations from MAS TRM reported to senior management and tracked to closure
MAS examination readiness — evidence packages maintained for regulatory inspection
DE-03.framework_reference: MAS TRM §5 (Technology Risk Management) — ongoing compliance monitoring

evidence_requirements: Audit log integrity protected — tamper-evident logging with access controls on log stores (MAS TRM §9.1)
Log integrity monitoring implemented — alerts on log deletion or modification events
Evidence preservation controls for regulatory investigation — legal hold capability documented
Log completeness validated periodically — gaps identified and remediated
Cyber incident response plan documented and tested annually — AI system incidents in scope (MAS TRM §10.1)
Automated containment capabilities for AI system compromise or harmful output scenarios
Incident response playbooks cover AI-specific scenarios: model poisoning, adversarial attack, data breach via AI
Response SLAs defined — containment and notification timelines for technology incidents
Escalation procedure for AI system incidents to senior management and board where material (MAS TRM §10.1)
Customer complaint and appeal mechanism for AI-assisted financial decisions
MAS incident notification: technology incidents affecting regulated services notified within 1 hour of declaration (MAS TRM §10.2)
Escalation chain tested — tabletop exercise or simulation records
RS-02.framework_reference: MAS TRM §10.1–10.2 (Incident Escalation and MAS Notification)

evidence_requirements: Forensic evidence preservation for cyber incidents — evidence integrity maintained for regulatory investigation (MAS TRM §10.1)
AI incident records preserved: model versions, input data, output logs, timeline
Evidence chain of custody documented for material incidents
Post-incident evidence package submitted to MAS on request — format and content standards documented
Business continuity plan (BCP) and IT disaster recovery plan (DRP) documented and tested for AI systems (MAS TRM §8.1)
AI model rollback capability — ability to revert to prior production model version within defined RTO
Recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) defined for AI-dependent services
BCP/DRP test results documented — AI system recovery tested at least annually
Post-incident review conducted for material technology incidents including AI system failures (MAS TRM §10.1)
Root cause analysis documented and remediation plan implemented with timeline
Lessons learned integrated into technology risk management framework
MAS post-incident report submitted for notifiable incidents — format and timeline per MAS TRM §10.2
RC-02.framework_reference: MAS TRM §10.1–10.2 (Post-Incident Review and Regulatory Reporting)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: Regulatory examination by MAS — periodic technology risk assessments and cyber resilience stress tests. MAS may conduct targeted examinations of AI system governance for FIs using AI in regulated functions. Annual self-assessment against MAS TRM by CIO/CISO.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). Notifiable technology incidents (affecting customer services, critical infrastructure, or data integrity) must be reported to MAS within 1 hour of declaration (MAS TRM §10.2) and followed up with a full incident report within 14 days.
reporting_obligations.notes: MAS adopts a risk-based supervisory approach. Severity of examination scrutiny scales with the FI's technology risk profile and systemic importance. AI-specific supervisory attention is increasing — MAS FEAT Principles (2018) and subsequent guidance are increasingly incorporated into MAS examination scope for FIs using AI in credit, fraud, and customer advisory functions.

human_oversight_mandates.description: MAS FEAT Principles (Fairness, Ethics, Accountability, Transparency) apply to Singapore FIs using AI/ML in customer-impacting decisions. Accountability principle requires human oversight and explainability for AI-assisted credit decisions, fraud alerts, and financial advice. MAS TRM §3.2 requires board oversight of technology risk — this extends to AI model risk for material deployments. Human escalation mandatory for AI incidents affecting customer services or regulatory obligations.
human_oversight_mandates.applies_to: AI systems used in credit assessment, fraud detection, customer advice, AML/KYC screening, and any function regulated by MAS that involves customer-facing AI decisions

notes: MAS TRM v2.0 — Technology Risk Management Guidelines issued January 2021 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. Mandatory for all MAS-regulated financial institutions. More prescriptive than the companion IMDA MGF (voluntary). This overlay applies MAS-specific evidence and threshold adjustments on top of the AKSI v0.6 common-control catalog. The prescriptive technical nature of MAS TRM means the mapped controls skew heavily toward full coverage across security, monitoring, vendor management, and incident response obligations. Evidence retention set to 1825 days (5 years) per MAS regulatory record-keeping expectations for financial services. Threshold adjustment on PR-05 log retention (1825 days) and RS-02 escalation notification (1 hour) reflects MAS-specific requirements more stringent than AKSI defaults. Companion overlay: imda-mgf.json for broader Singapore AI governance context. MAS FEAT Principles (2018) referenced for AI-specific accountability and fairness obligations — these are soft-law guidance but increasingly examined by MAS for material AI deployments. v0.2 planned to incorporate FEAT Principles as explicit framework mapping entries and add Singapore PDPA Article-level citations for PR-04.
